messages:
samir: Heads up — p95 for text-generation API jumped ~2.5x in the canary after runtime v2.14 rolled at 09:02 UTC. Not global, mostly tenant cohort 'marketplace' and seq_len 512-1024. Anyone looking?

lia: saw it on the dashboard ~09:10. p99 up too but less pronounced. Spike correlates with increased batching size metrics and some long-tail queueing on hotpath nodes.

kevin: @samir do you have a couple of trace IDs? I can pull low-level traces from the canary pool.

samir: putting a couple here: trace/abc123, trace/def456. Backend logs show many requests sitting in batch-assemble for ~120ms before kernel run. Example snippet:```json
{"request_id":"abc123","stage":"batch_assemble","duration_ms":118}```

ella: that batch_assemble time is suspicious. v2.14 changed the batching threshold policy (adaptive thresholding to favor throughput). Looks like for mid-size seqs it overbatches and causes head-of-line waiting.

lia: also noticed increased LRU evictions in KV cache on those nodes — possibly more cache misses are increasing effective compute time per request, so batches wait for outstanding KV loads.

kevin: repro steps I used locally:
1) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"<512 tokens>...","max_tokens":128}' -v
2) repeat with ~200 concurrent clients using hey/ab to reproduce p95 uptick

samir: confirmed repro at scale in canary via load harness. Short-term mitigation I propose: revert adaptive thresholding to conservatively sized static threshold used in v2.13 for canary nodes, and reduce max batch size from 64->32.

ella: addendum: we can also add a targeted routing rule to steer 'marketplace' tenant traffic to v2.13 until we fully validate. That avoids global rollback.

kevin: agree. I'll open a quick rollback PR for canary config (not kernel) and push a routing override for the cohort. ETA ~15m.

infra-bot: deploy started: rollback-config/canary-thresholds -> in_progress. CI checks okay.

lia: while rollback is happening, can someone collect the following for postmortem?
- full timeline of batching changes (who/why)
- batch size distribution histograms pre/post
- KV cache hit/miss by tenant
- traces for top 10 slow batches

samir: collecting now. linking trace dump when done.

kevin: rollback finished, routing override live. Early telemetry looks promising — p95 trending down in the canary after ~2m. Will monitor 30m before rolling to prod. :thumbsup:

ella: nice. Once stable let's run an A/B with a smaller adaptive threshold and extra KV cache warmup steps (prefetch popular keys) to see if we can keep throughput without hurting tail.

samir: agreed. Temporary follow-ups: create a short runbook entry for this class of regression (batch threshold interactions), add an alert for batch_assemble > 80ms, and add tenant-cohort tagging on metric exports.

kevin: filing JIRA INF-4723 with rollback, telemetry, and follow-up tasks.

lia: thanks all. Will keep monitoring. If p95 climbs again we escalate to rollback across the pool.

samir: FYI traces and CSV dumps uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/canary/3187654321/ (links in the incident ticket).
